concerns: Inference-risk: Affinity depletion may remove or damage bona fide EV surface proteins or subpopulations, producing artifactual improvement in marker co-localization rather than true enrichment (proposal notes this competing explanation; MISEV supports caution).
Assay-interference: Depletion buffer components or resin leachables could confound immuno-capture or protection assays unless explicitly validated (proposal lists this dependency).

Yield/scalability uncertainty: No supplied evidence shows that depletion resins/flowthrough modalities at scale will preserve low-shear conditions and acceptable recoveries; manufacturability statements are inferential and unproven.

Translatability limitation: Improved analytical co-localization does not guarantee improved in vivo detectability or delivery—Driedonks2022 underscores species/formulation-dependent biodistribution limitations; this limits claims about downstream detectability or efficacy.

Missing controls: The canonical evidence set does not include program-specific capture-compatibility controls or spike-in recovery data for the proposed depletion buffers—these are required to exclude buffer-mediated assay artifacts.
conclusion: Supported in part. The proposal’s rationale and proposed measurement strategy are appropriately aligned with the cited canonical evidence (MISEV2023, Hermann2023, Driedonks2022) and correctly label the key statements as inferences. However, there is no direct experimental evidence in the provided canonical set that pre-SEC affinity depletion (implemented under low-shear, low-salt conditions) preserves EV membrane integrity or reproducibly improves particle recovery versus the TFF->SEC->cushion comparator; that is an explicit evidence gap that must be resolved experimentally. Key risks (removal of EV-associated proteins, assay interference from depletion buffers/resin leachables, and uncertain translatability to in vivo detectability) are identified in the proposal and are consistent with the cited guidance and limiting biodistribution data.
evidence_gap: No direct experimental evidence in the supplied canonical set demonstrates that a gentle pre-SEC affinity-depletion step (as proposed) preserves membrane-protected EV markers and yields equal-or-improved recovered particle mass versus the TFF->SEC->cushion workflow; the program-specific head-to-head data (pre-SEC depletion + SEC vs TFF->SEC->cushion) using the orthogonal capture+protection and yield metrics is missing.
